attractions.name: Christ the Redeemer & Sugarloaf
attractions.desc: Rio's two signature viewpoints offer different perspectives on the same sprawling city: Christ the Redeemer's outstretched arms atop Corcovado Mountain, and Sugarloaf's cable car ascent over the harbor. Both are best done on separate, clear days given how weather-dependent the views are. The statue, completed in 1931, remains one of the most recognized monuments in the world.

attractions.name: Iguazu Falls
attractions.desc: A wider, arguably more dramatic set of falls than Niagara, spanning nearly three kilometers along the Brazil–Argentina border with roughly 275 individual cascades. The Brazilian side offers panoramic views of the full falls system, while the Argentine side allows closer approaches to individual cascades. A boat tour to the base of the Devil's Throat, the falls' most powerful section, offers a soaking, adrenaline-filled perspective.

attractions.name: Amazon lodges near Manaus
attractions.desc: River cruises and jungle walks from lodges reachable only by boat give access to the world's largest rainforest, with night canoe trips revealing caimans and other nocturnal wildlife. The 'meeting of waters', where the dark Rio Negro and sandy-colored Amazon River flow side by side without mixing for several kilometers, is a striking natural phenomenon near the city. Manaus itself, once wealthy from the rubber boom, retains grand period architecture including an ornate opera house.

attractions.name: Pelourinho, Salvador
attractions.desc: Colonial architecture and Afro-Brazilian culture define Brazil's former capital, its cobbled squares once the site of a slave market and now a UNESCO World Heritage Site celebrating Afro-Brazilian heritage. Capoeira demonstrations and live percussion are common sights in its plazas. Salvador's cuisine, particularly dishes rooted in West African tradition, reflects the city's deep cultural connections across the Atlantic.

attractions.name: Copacabana & Ipanema beaches
attractions.desc: Rio's two most famous beaches stretch along a dense urban coastline, their promenades a hub for football, volleyball, and people-watching throughout the day. The iconic wave-patterned sidewalk mosaic along Copacabana was designed by landscape architect Roberto Burle Marx. Sunset at Ipanema's Arpoador rock is a popular local tradition, often met with spontaneous applause from the crowd.

attractions.name: Pantanal wetlands
attractions.desc: The world's largest tropical wetland, offering wildlife viewing that many consider even more reliable than the denser Amazon rainforest, since animals are easier to spot in the open terrain. Jaguar sightings, rare and difficult elsewhere, are relatively common here during the dry season. Boat and jeep safaris reveal capybaras, caimans, and an enormous diversity of birdlife across the flooded plains.

itinerary.label: Days 1–4
itinerary.title: Rio de Janeiro
itinerary.desc: Christ the Redeemer, Sugarloaf, and beach time at Ipanema and Copacabana.
itinerary.cost: Christ the Redeemer entry (with the van or train up) costs about BRL 100–150; the Sugarloaf cable car runs about BRL 150–200.
itinerary.food: Try a proper feijoada lunch on a Saturday — it's traditionally served then, and many local spots do it best on that specific day.

itinerary.label: Days 5–6
itinerary.title: Iguazu Falls
itinerary.desc: Walkways on the Brazilian side and a boat ride to the base of the falls.
itinerary.cost: Brazilian-side park entry costs about BRL 85 for foreigners; the boat ride to the base of the falls costs extra, around BRL 250–300.
itinerary.food: Grab a quick pastel (fried pastry snack) at a park cafe — a common, affordable Brazilian bite.

itinerary.label: Days 7–10
itinerary.title: Amazon or Salvador
itinerary.desc: Either a lodge stay near Manaus or an extension to Salvador's old town.
itinerary.logistics: ~2h flight from Iguazu via São Paulo
itinerary.cost: A multi-day Amazon lodge stay near Manaus runs $150–400+/night depending on comfort level, usually including meals and excursions.
itinerary.food: In Salvador, try acarajé, a deep-fried black-eyed pea fritter sold by street vendors — a genuine Bahian specialty.

goodToKnow.tipping: 10% is often already added as a service charge in restaurants
goodToKnow.safety: Use normal city caution, especially at night; resorts and main tourist areas are well set up
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Domestic flights are essential given the country's size
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Rio de Janeiro's Galeão International (GIG) is the main gateway for this route

faq.q: Do I need a visa for Brazil?
faq.a: It depends on your nationality: EU and UK citizens remain visa-free for short stays, but as of April 2025, US, Canadian, and Australian citizens need an e-visa (about $80.90, applied for online in advance at the official portal) — a real change from the previous visa-free arrangement.

faq.q: Which airport should I fly into?
faq.a: Rio de Janeiro's Galeão International (GIG) for this route.

faq.q: Do I need vaccinations for Brazil?
faq.a: Yellow fever vaccination is recommended, and sometimes required depending on your itinerary and origin, if visiting the Amazon specifically. It's not needed for Rio or Iguazu alone.
Generally good value by Western standards, though Rio's beachfront areas and peak Carnival season run notably higher.

daysReason: 10 days covers Rio de Janeiro, Iguazu Falls, and either the Amazon or Salvador without rushing, given Brazil's enormous size. 6–7 works for just Rio and Iguazu; 14+ lets you comfortably add both the Amazon and Salvador instead of choosing one.
visa: EU and UK citizens remain visa-free for short stays, but as of April 2025, US, Canadian, and Australian citizens need an e-visa applied for online in advance — always confirm current rules before booking.

attractions.name: Cristo Redentor e Pão de Açúcar
attractions.desc: As duas vistas assinatura do Rio oferecem perspetivas diferentes sobre a mesma cidade extensa: os braços abertos do Cristo Redentor no topo do Monte Corcovado, e a subida de teleférico do Pão de Açúcar sobre o porto. Ambos são melhor feitos em dias claros separados dado quão dependentes do tempo são as vistas. A estátua, concluída em 1931, continua a ser um dos monumentos mais reconhecidos do mundo.

attractions.name: Cataratas do Iguaçu
attractions.desc: Um conjunto mais largo, indiscutivelmente mais dramático de cataratas do que o Niágara, estendendo-se por quase três quilómetros ao longo da fronteira Brasil-Argentina com cerca de 275 cascatas individuais. O lado brasileiro oferece vistas panorâmicas de todo o sistema de cataratas, enquanto o lado argentino permite aproximações mais próximas a cascatas individuais. Um passeio de barco até à base da Garganta do Diabo, a secção mais poderosa das cataratas, oferece uma perspetiva encharcada e cheia de adrenalina.

attractions.name: Lodges na Amazónia perto de Manaus
attractions.desc: Cruzeiros fluviais e caminhadas na selva a partir de lodges alcançáveis apenas de barco dão acesso à maior floresta tropical do mundo, com passeios noturnos de canoa a revelar jacarés e outra vida selvagem noturna. O 'encontro das águas', onde o escuro Rio Negro e o Rio Amazonas de cor arenosa correm lado a lado sem se misturar durante vários quilómetros, é um fenómeno natural marcante perto da cidade. A própria Manaus, outrora rica graças ao boom da borracha, mantém arquitetura de época grandiosa incluindo uma ornamentada casa de ópera.

attractions.name: Pelourinho, Salvador
attractions.desc: Arquitetura colonial e cultura afro-brasileira definem a antiga capital do Brasil, com as suas praças de calçada, outrora local de um mercado de escravos e hoje Património Mundial da UNESCO celebrando a herança afro-brasileira. Demonstrações de capoeira e percussão ao vivo são vistas comuns nas suas praças. A cozinha de Salvador, particularmente pratos com raízes na tradição da África Ocidental, reflete as profundas ligações culturais da cidade através do Atlântico.

attractions.name: Praias de Copacabana e Ipanema
attractions.desc: As duas praias mais famosas do Rio estendem-se ao longo de uma densa costa urbana, com os seus passeios a servirem de polo para futebol, voleibol, e observação de gente ao longo do dia. O icónico mosaico de calçada em padrão de onda ao longo de Copacabana foi desenhado pelo arquiteto paisagista Roberto Burle Marx. O pôr do sol na rocha de Arpoador em Ipanema é uma tradição local popular, muitas vezes recebida com aplausos espontâneos da multidão.

attractions.name: Zonas húmidas do Pantanal
attractions.desc: A maior zona húmida tropical do mundo, oferecendo observação de vida selvagem que muitos consideram ainda mais fiável do que a mais densa floresta amazónica, já que os animais são mais fáceis de avistar em terreno aberto. Avistamentos de onças, raros e difíceis noutros lugares, são relativamente comuns aqui durante a época seca. Safaris de barco e jipe revelam capivaras, jacarés, e uma enorme diversidade de aves pelas planícies inundadas.

itinerary.label: Dias 1–4
itinerary.title: Rio de Janeiro
itinerary.desc: Cristo Redentor, Pão de Açúcar, e tempo de praia em Ipanema e Copacabana.

itinerary.label: Dias 5–6
itinerary.title: Cataratas do Iguaçu
itinerary.desc: Passadiços no lado brasileiro e um passeio de barco até à base das cataratas.

itinerary.label: Dias 7–10
itinerary.title: Amazónia ou Salvador
itinerary.desc: Ou uma estadia em lodge perto de Manaus, ou uma extensão à cidade antiga de Salvador.
itinerary.logistics: ~2h de voo desde Iguaçu via São Paulo
